summary: A fanout wave lands one ledger commit per pick and the handoff keeps only the last, under a hover calling it the produced commit — a chain wanting the rest has no surface

per.section: A fact the engine holds is reported, never rediscovered

acceptance: a wave that shipped N entries reports every ledger commit it landed on the surface a handoff reads, and the hover on the single-sha field states which commit that is rather than "the produced commit", so a chain reading a fanout wave's ship is not handed the last of N as if it were the whole
tests: a fanout wave that shipped two entries reports both ledger commits it landed
